summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator

What we developed: We built a simple Python tool that helps choose safe and useful landing sites on the Moon. It divides a lunar region into a grid of small squares and checks three things for each one: slope, sunlight, and distance to water ice. Squares steeper than 10 degrees are removed as unsafe. The rest are scored (40% slope, 30% sunlight, 30% ice), and the tool picks the top five sites and draws a heatmap. Our prototype uses sample data, and real NASA LRO terrain data can be added next.

How it addresses the challenge: Landing site selection means balancing many factors at once. Our tool turns this into a clear process: filter out unsafe areas, score the rest, and rank them. The weights can be changed to suit different missions, for example more weight on sunlight for solar-powered landers. The heatmap makes results easy to understand, and the code is open on GitHub for others to test and improve.

Why it is important: Landing is one of the riskiest parts of a mission, and a poor site can cause failure. With more missions planned to the Moon’s south pole, where water ice may exist, careful site selection matters more than ever. Our project shows how simple data analytics can support real space decisions.
details:
What does your project do and how does it work?
It finds safe landing sites on the Moon. It splits the surface into a grid, removes steep squares, scores the rest, and ranks the top 5.

What benefit does it have?
It makes landing site choice faster, clearer, and safer.

What is the intended impact?
To reduce landing risk and help plan missions to the Moon’s south pole, where water ice may exist.

What tools did you use?
Python, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, and GitHub.

How is your project creative?
It turns a hard space decision into a simple score and heatmap that anyone can understand. The weights can be changed for different missions.

What factors did your team consider?
Slope (safety), sunlight (solar power), and distance to water ice (resources).
